doc.title: Keter Betts interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 11, 1996

title: Touring with Bostic and the one-nighter circuit
summary: Three-month tours of dance one-nighters across the South and West through regional bookers like Weinberg and Robey, including Bostic's first California trip.

story.theme_name: Life on the road: touring bands, buses and one-nighters
story.community_name: Life on the road: buses, trains and one-nighters

blocks.x: Boy, talk about starting on the top. Did you ever have any trouble with that particular group like traveling in different parts of the country?
Oh, everybody did. You know I mean that’s the way it was.

It was standard, but I had not been exposed to that. I used to go down and sometimes spend a summer I guess I did it about five times with my great grandmother, who was in Wilmington, North Carolina, but I was too young to understand that because you know we never really had to go out from a certain area. And going down by train there was a Traveler’s Aid, I think you wore a little button or something like that and you’d stop in Philadelphia and someone would come on and make sure you got some milk and cookies

or something, and get to wash. They’d take care of you, you know. So when I went with Bostic, we would go out sometimes like three months, we’d do it sometimes twice a year — three month tour. And one-nighters. And there was an old man from Pittsburgh, no from Pennsylvania called Weinberg, and you’d do the Weinberg tour.

He was the agent. And he booked from Washington on down, West Virginia, Virginia, North Carolina, South Carolina, that was all his territory. And you would go down to Florida, and then Rick Robey was the Florida area, and around to New Orleans. No Weinberg was from there. Rick Robey was in New Orleans and that area in there, and then you got up to Don Robey was in Texas and so forth. And sometimes we’d be in Texas three weeks. I mean that’s how long it takes you to get out of Texas.

These were dances, yeah. No concerts. And we finally went to California in 1950, and that was Bostic’s first time there. And then went up to San Francisco and then up through [inaudible] and you’d come back the northern route where you would do Salt Lake City, Denver, Chicago and come through Ohio, and sometimes it’d be a three month tour.
